scope: tcConnect bounded SDK disconnect/modal waits and timeout quarantine; exact tcHandleWallet initial quarantine guard
assessment: Each disconnect, openModal and obsolete closeModal SDK wait is bounded by its own 8000 ms Promise.race, with a completion-time elapsed/backward-clock guard and timer cleanup.

Timeout quarantines the uncancellable singleton via the existing availability flag, clears connection intent, invalidates the recipient generation and releases preparation/button ownership in the outer finally. New SDK attempts require page reload; manual recipient input remains available.

Exact initial tcHandleWallet quarantine guard suppresses both late wallet status and late null disconnect callbacks. Timeout calls tcInvalidateRecipient to increment recipient generation, so an in-flight verification fails its existing tcRecipientState equality guard before applying its result.
Late SDK promise resolution/rejection has no application continuation after the losing race. SDK-internal side effects are not cancelled, so quarantine intentionally persists for the page lifetime.
Current timeout feedback explicitly asks for reload or manual input; it does not promise SDK cancellation. Stale attempts do not publish timeout feedback.
Scope guard accepts only tcConnect body changes plus the exact initial tcHandleWallet guard; mutations to the remaining verification handler and other application functions are rejected.

Read-only live preflight passed: 58 input hashes, four unchanged runtime states, target metadata and exact substituted public template. Nineteen local scope/drift/apply/reconcile/rollback checks passed; rehearsal touched only temporary files.
limitations: SDK promises remain uncancellable; a late internal modal side effect can still occur. Reload is required to establish a fresh SDK instance after timeout.
Payload request response/body wait remains the existing AbortController-based behavior and is outside this SDK wait slice.
